findings.summary: the strip added for idempotence sits below the early return at line 666, so a launch that seeded no server (unfenced, resumed, or holding the operator's settings) keeps whatever anchored instruction the prompt already carried, naming tools that launch does not have
findings.text: non-blocking: reckon/crew/prompts.py:666 returns the prompt untouched whenever backend['anchored_edit'] is not True, and prompt_without_anchored_edit_instruction is only reached at line 696. The docstring at line 665 states the rule without that qualification - 'An instruction already present is removed first, so a lane change that composes from a prompt file a launch already wrote keeps exactly one' - while dispatch_sessions.py:1632 _lane_prompt reads that prompt file verbatim and appends the coordinator advice after it. So a fresh-session lane change onto a launch that did not seed the server (the test_a_treated_run_resumes_with_builtin_tools_and_a_false_receipt shape) hands the worker an instruction to use read_anchored and edit_anchored while the built-in tools are the ones registered. It is recoverable - the built-in edits are no longer disallowed on that launch, so the worker falls back - which is why it does not hold the node, but the stale block should be stripped on the ineligible path too, and the docstring should name the qualification if it is not.

findings.summary: the idempotence fix's load-bearing production case is codex, but the only case guarding it is claude-shaped, so a strip regression on the codex path is unasserted
findings.text: non-blocking: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3050 appends the codex instruction at dispatch time and then passes that same prompt into reckon/_backends.py:3119 at line 3391-3394, so without the strip at reckon/crew/prompts.py:697 EVERY codex dispatch now carries two copies - the widest-reaching instance of the defect the prior review found. tests/test_anchored_edit_claude_arm.py:233 test_a_prompt_already_instructed_keeps_one_copy exercises only the claude body and only on the launch path, and the negative control's -k selection (negative-control.log) shows that case still passing under the mutation, so nothing reddens if the codex strip alone is removed. The claude case does guard the function, which is why this is not blocking, but the codex arm deserves the same single-case assertion; tests/test_anchored_edit_codex_arm.py already owns that surface.
